title: Lesson 32: Flow Architecture: Flow vs Apex vs External Automation, Decision Framework
description: A repeatable framework for placing a process: Record-Triggered Flow for low density, a Flow plus invocable Apex hybrid for medium density, Apex triggers for high density, and external automation for reasoning and cross-system work.

questions.question: A process must coordinate Salesforce with an external planning system and a separate warehouse system, each with a different payload. Where does the orchestration belong?
options: In a record-triggered flow on the Salesforce object, so that the whole handoff stays inside the org itself.
In an Apex trigger, because only Apex can call out to an external system.
In the external layer, with Salesforce publishing an event and the coordinator driving the rest.
In a scheduled flow that polls the other systems on a fixed recurring interval.
questions.explanation: Orchestration across systems that Salesforce does not own belongs in the layer that owns them, so the platform publishes the business event and lets the external layer coordinate the rest.

questions.question: A finance process must commit its work or roll the whole change back if a boundary check fails. Which home fits and why?
options: Flow, because it offers a built-in rollback step for this case.
Apex, because Flow has no savepoint or rollback for partial-commit control.
Either one, because Flow and Apex express transaction control equally well.
External automation, because transaction control is a cross-system concern.
questions.explanation: Savepoint, rollback, and partial commit are capabilities Flow does not expose, so a transactional-control requirement is an Apex requirement rather than a Flow shortcoming to work around.

questions.question: An object carries fifteen to thirty automations, moderate batch volumes, coupled parent and child updates, and some recursion risk. Which standard fits?
options: A hybrid: keep the record-triggered flow as the entry point and move the compute into invocable Apex.
One very large record-triggered flow that handles every single rule the team could think of on that object.
A full migration to an Apex trigger behind a metadata framework.
External automation, since any risk of recursion is really a cross-system problem.
questions.explanation: Medium density is the hybrid case: the flow keeps one readable, ordered entry point while the compute Flow handles poorly moves behind an invocable Apex seam.
